The company argues that years of development, a growing production base, and expanding use cases have strengthened its position in a market still shaped by slow vehicle approvals and shifting electric vehicle strategies.

items.title: Optical PD volume production lifts WIN Semiconductors' Q2 revenue 39% YoY
items.summary: WIN Semiconductors, a gallium arsenide (GaAs) foundry, reported consolidated revenue of NT$5.26 billion (US$178 million) for the second quarter of 2026, up 14.5% sequentially and 39% year over year, driven by improved product mix, higher shipment volumes and the ramp-up of new products.

items.title: Samsung and Hyundai target Silicon Valley AI roundtable
items.summary: Samsung Electronics chairman Lee Jae-Yong and Hyundai Motor chairman Chung Eui-Sun are reportedly moving to join the advisory network of the global AI leaders' gathering "Silicon Valley & The World." The two are expected to meet AI industry leaders, including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, in San Francisco this week, before possibly meeting again in Silicon Valley in November 2026.

items.title: Alphabet's purchase commitments surge past US$800 billion amid AI infrastructure expansion
items.summary: Alphabet disclosed in its latest quarterly filing that its purchase commitments and other contractual obligations had climbed to US$811 billion as of the end of June, underscoring the company's aggressive push to secure long-term AI infrastructure capacity.

items.title: KKR plans gradual exit as LCY Group accelerates semiconductor materials expansion
items.summary: TSMC supplier LCY Group President Bowei Lee said private equity firm KKR & Co. plans to gradually divest its holdings in businesses affiliated with the Taiwanese chemical group, a move he believes will give the company greater flexibility to accelerate its expansion in semiconductor materials.

items.title: Russia adopts low-cost navigation workaround for Molniya attack drones
items.summary: Russia has equipped low-cost Molniya attack drones with a civilian compass and camera-based reading system to keep them on course when satellite navigation is jammed or unavailable, according to a Ukrainian defense adviser. The modification underscores how electronic warfare continues to shape the Russia-Ukraine battlefield and how Moscow is seeking inexpensive ways to preserve drone effectiveness.

items.title: Lynas says Malaysia heavy rare earth project has gone over budget
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths said its heavy rare earth expansion in Malaysia has gone over budget as the Australia-based miner works to build out a non-China supply chain. The disclosure came alongside the latest quarterly results for the period ended June 30, 2026, in which revenue reached AU$289 million (US$202 million), up 70% year on year and the strongest level in four years.

items.title: Pantheon Electric expands copper platform as AI and grid demand tighten supply
items.summary: Pantheon Electric said it has completed the acquisition of four manufacturers and built an integrated power infrastructure platform across 21 factories in North America and Europe. The company said the expansion came as AI data centers, grid upgrades, and US manufacturing drove stronger demand for copper-based infrastructure.

items.title: Google AI search reshapes traffic as publishers weigh blocking crawlers
items.summary: Google's expansion of AI-driven search features is prompting a backlash from publishers and media companies that rely on search traffic. Over the past year, the company has rolled out AI Mode across search pages, using its Gemini chatbot to deliver direct answers that can keep users on Google instead of sending them to outside sites.

items.title: Airbus raises profit outlook as supply bottlenecks ease
items.summary: Airbus updated its financial outlook for investors, saying easing supply-chain constraints should support stronger production and profit growth through 2029. According to Bloomberg, the European planemaker now expects adjusted annual operating profit of EUR12 billion-EUR13 billion (US$13.71 billion-US$14.84 billion) by 2029, nearly double current levels, and it plans a EUR5 billion (US$5.71 billion) share buyback over the next three years.

items.title: 89 fabs by 2030, 50 more by 2035: chip industry spreads risk through global collab
items.summary: AI infrastructure investment is reaching unprecedented levels, with estimates showing it will lift global semiconductor output past US$1 trillion in 2026, four years earlier than previously expected, and expand the market to US$1.5 trillion by 2030. items.title: South Korea unveils AI cooperation agenda as Nvidia partnerships expand
items.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung launched an AI-focused visit to Silicon Valley by announcing a "San Francisco AI Declaration" aimed at promoting international cooperation in artificial intelligence, while a series of technology partnerships involving Nvidia, South Korean companies and US firms were announced alongside the visit, according to The Chosun Daily, Reuters, and Bloomberg.

items.title: South Korean leaders meet Nvidia as AI partnerships expand
items.summary: South Korean President Jae Myung Lee, senior government officials, business executives, and researchers gathered in San Francisco this week for an AI summit with Nvidia and industry partners, highlighting South Korea's efforts to strengthen its artificial intelligence ecosystem and expand international collaboration.

items.title: Intel, China-based Lens Technology partner to explore glass substrate semiconductor packaging
items.summary: Intel Corporation and Lens Technology have announced a strategic collaboration to explore the development of advanced semiconductor packaging technologies using glass substrates. The companies said the initiative aims to support future computing platforms by improving performance, increasing interconnect density, and enhancing power efficiency.

items.title: PCs & Smartphones Supply Constrained
items.summary:
Global unit shipments of PCs and smartphones were both down versus a year ago in the 2nd quarter of 2026, according to IDC. PCs were down 4.9% and smartphones were down 6.7%. Both PCs and smartphones showed growth in 2024 and 2025. IDC is predicting an 11.3% decline in PCs and a 13.9% decline in smartphones in 2026.
